messages:
alex: Quick q — seeing odd behavior with header-based routing + model affinity. Tenant passed X-Model-Pref and X-Model-Version; gateway returned a quantized fallback that wasn't compatibility-checked. Is header -> strict pin or best-effort?
maya: We treat model alias pins as intent, not a guarantee. Headers shouldn't bypass compatibility. If alias resolves to incompatible model, gateway should pick next compatible candidate or error if pin is strict.
kevin: FYI the gateway currently short-circuits when header matches exact model id. If model removed or incompatible (seq length, ops), it falls back to cheapest compatible model but we drop the "pin" telemetry tag. Not ideal. :confused:
sam: Console UX note — we have a "force pin" toggle in rollouts. Does API header pin map 1:1 to that? If not, users will be surprised when console says pinned but API doesn't honor.
rupert: Proposal: evaluation order should be: explicit model-id -> alias pin (resolved to candidate set) -> route selector. ALWAYS run compatibility filter (seq, ops, quant) before finalizing. Also attach routing.origin=header and routing.pin_mode={strict|prefer|best_effort} to telemetry.
alex: Example of what I hacked locally:
```yaml
match:
  headers:
    X-Model-Pref: /redwood-.*/
action:
  resolve_alias: true
  enforce_compatibility: true
  telemetry_tags: ["header:pref"]
```
thoughts?
kevin: Two operational gotchas: 1) quotas/reserved capacity — if alias resolves to a Dedicated-only model and tenant lacks commit we should 403 not silently fallback. 2) header pins can be used to evade route quotas unless we account for pin origin in rate/quota accounting.
maya: Add a "pin_strictness" param to routing action: strict|prefer|best_effort. Default to prefer. Console force-pin overrides to strict. Also make compatibility failures return structured reason codes for alerting.
sam: UX: console needs to surface when a header could override a console pin and when a pin is best-effort. Show "request-level pin used" banner and a link to per-route docs. Also expose telemetry flag to show billing impact of header pins. :eyes:
infra-bot: deploy-check: routing-eval-tests failed 2/42 — seq_length_filter missing in new alias resolver. Logs: https://ci.internal/reports/2250012345 :warning:
rupert: I'll take the infra fix. Plan: resolver returns candidate list + compatibility vector (pass/fail + reason codes). Add quota-check step after resolution; if strict pin and quota fails -> 403 with JSON error {"code":"PIN_QUOTA","msg":"tenant lacks commit for pinned model"}. Also add telemetry fields: routing.source=header, routing.pin_mode, routing.resolve_reasons.
alex: Agreed. TL;DR: implement early compatibility filter, introduce pin_strictness, enforce quota checks for strict pins, and wire telemetry tags so dashboards/showrollouts can differentiate header vs console pins. I'll draft the API + migration RFC and push tests. :thumbsup:
rupert: will open PR for resolver + tests, tag you all.
kevin: thanks — will add quota-side checks in billing client.
maya: once PRs land I'll update the telemetry dashboards to include pin origin breakdown.
sam: will add console copy and flag changes to rollout UX — will stub screenshots.
